text: It brings people together and, if we think about it, it forms a significant part of our daily shared lived experience.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: A bad commuting experience can disrupt your mood and day, almost as much as a domestic dispute at home.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, this is why people feel so strongly about the quality, reliability and experience of travelling.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Panel has, therefore, recommended enhancing the travel experience through greater connectivity and better service for everyone.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Panel also understood that there is, ultimately, a limit to infrastructure building on our tiny island.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Panel has proposed a bold new vision of a healthy and safe 20-minute town travel and a 45-Minute City travel for everyone by 2040.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary will elaborate on LTMP 2040 later.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I agree with Mr Sitoh Yih Pin and Assoc Prof Walter Theseira that we need to exercise fiscal discipline in order to reduce costs and maximise value for money.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: First, always look out for novel design solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This depot is going to be a 4-in-1, with three MRT depots for the East-West Line, Downtown Line and the upcoming TEL, which are stacked one on top of another, and there is also a bus depot for 760 buses.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is the first such facility of its kind.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: LTA’s engineers have also saved more than $3 billion in potential construction costs by shifting the depot and the reception tracks for the Cross Island Line above ground.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The second way is to always look at lifecycle costs when procuring major assets that will operate for decades.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: When the first-generation North-South and East-West Line trains were due for renewal, LTA challenged the train manufacturers to design systems using the latest technology that would be easier and cheaper to maintain throughout the 30-year lifecycle of the trains.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Third, leverage competitive market forces wherever appropriate and whenever possible.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Fourth, incentivise – and you will notice I use the word "incentivise" – commuters to change their behavior where possible and where convenient in order to optimise the overall performance of the system.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is something which I think Assoc Prof Walter Theseira has been pursuing for quite some time.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I have noticed his speeches in this Chamber and he has asked about differential fares.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: These were introduced by PTC in December 2017.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: If we strip away the jargon, actually this is about saving money and improving the travel experience by encouraging more rail commuters to travel during off-peak hours.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will continue to look for ways to smoothen out these peaks and troughs which, Assoc Prof Theseira, as an economist, will tell you have a very important impact on overall long-term system costs but, at the same time, improves the travelling experience for people, as it is less crowded.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It does so in a positive way through differential fares.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But even as we do this, we need to be mindful that not all commuters have the flexibility to change their commuting patterns.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Even with such measures in place, the brutal hard truth is that a high-quality public transport system still requires significant resources.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The perennial question – and it is a political question as well – remains "How do we strike the right balance between the costs borne by taxpayers, commuters and operators?" I emphasised "taxpayers" because every dollar that the Government puts into the public transport system ultimately comes from taxpayers.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, remember there is always a balancing act that is necessary.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: On the Government's side – and that means, on the taxpayers' side of the equation – we will continue to keep fares affordable by fully funding all infrastructure costs and providing significant operating subsidies.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is why, despite the improvements in capacity and reliability, public transport actually has become more affordable.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is inevitable that fares will have to keep pace with costs.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In 2018, PTC introduced a Network Capacity Factor into the fare formula.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Dennis Tan also referred to this in his intervention earlier.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Basically, this factor allows the fares to be adjusted in tandem with capacity changes of our public transport network relative to commuter demand.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: What I am trying to say in simple terms is this, that we would all like to increase capacity to make it more convenient and improve the travel experience.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But all of us here also know that an increase in capacity comes with an increase in cost.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I would like, however, to assure Mr Dennis Tan that we will certainly calibrate the expansion of rail capacity so that it expands in tandem with ridership growth.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is not feasible anyway to have unlimited expansion in capacity, and I am sure that the impact of NCF will be managed in due course.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Dennis Tan also suggested factoring in service quality.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is another example where I agree with his intention.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I think the divergence is in the method.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Service standards, including on-time performance reliability, are already regulated through existing frameworks.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But these frameworks are outside the fare formula.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In other words, these standards are imposed by LTA on the operators as conditions for service.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In addition, operators can be penalised for breach of regulatory standards or breach of licence conditions and the penalties paid are calibrated to ensure fairness and accountability.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The penalties paid accrue to the Public Transport Fund which, as all Members know, is then redistributed, especially to the lower-income families.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is used, therefore, to provide financial assistance on the one hand, but also to serve as a disincentive against the operators taking shortcuts.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Dennis Tan also suggested factoring operators' profitability into the fare formula.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The profitability of PTOs, in fact, is already taken into consideration in the fare review mechanism.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: For example, the productivity gains of PTOs are shared with commuters through the Productivity Extraction Factor in the fare formula.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: If Members look up the briefing, it is in there in the formula.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I think PTC will happily have this conversation with Members offline.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The operators also contribute a portion of the fare increase into the Public Transport Fund.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Typically, they contribute about 20%-50% of the expected increase in fare revenue for that year, with the more profitable PTOs contributing more.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This puts in place a formal mechanism for the PTOs to share their gains with commuters.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: PTC has done well and I am confident it will continue to strike the right balance.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The key word here is "balance" – balance between fare affordability and the long-term fiscal sustainability of our public transport system.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I spoke last week in my capacity as the Minister for Foreign Affairs on managing relations with Malaysia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As Members know, several transport-related issues have arisen – the Kuala Lumpur-Singapore High Speed Rail (HSR) project.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Then, there was the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System Link (RTS Link) project, as well as the airspace and maritime boundary issues.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have upheld international law and we respected the sanctity of international agreements.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: At the same time, we have been reasonable, we have been constructive in trying to resolve issues in a win-win manner.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, this is a case in point.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In August last year, Malaysia requested to defer the HSR project.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In the spirit of bilateral cooperation, we agreed to Malaysia's request, and both sides agreed to a two-year suspension up to 31 May 2020.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Malaysia has requested that during the suspension period, both sides discuss the way forward for the HSR Project, with the aim of reducing the overall costs.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have yet to receive any new proposals from Malaysia on this, but we will certainly study any such proposals carefully when we receive them.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We look forward to working with Malaysia when the project resumes.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: On the RTS Link, this is another rail project that we have with Malaysia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And it was Mr Ang Wei Neng who quite rightly pointed out that the RTS Link should significantly ease congestion at our land checkpoints which, by the way, are the busiest land checkpoints in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This will make it much more convenient for people to travel between Singapore and Johor Bahru.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Minister Khaw Boon Wan updated the House in January that the RTS Link project has seen some delays.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore fully expects both countries to fully abide by this obligation and has made this clear to Malaysia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Whilst emphasising the obligation of both Governments to call a fair, open and transparent international tender to appoint the OpCo, but in the spirit of bilateral cooperation, Singapore has been willing to engage Malaysia on its proposals for Malaysia's Joint Venture (JV) partner for the RTS Link OpCo.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Unfortunately, Malaysia has repeatedly delayed confirming its JV partner for the RTS Link OpCo.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We hope that they will reach a decision soon.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore continues to believe that the RTS Link is a mutually beneficial project, and I would like to assure Mr Ang Wei Neng that we remain fully committed to implementing the project as per the RTS Link Bilateral Agreement.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have also been engaging Malaysia in order to find constructive solutions to both maritime and airspace issues.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This purported extension goes beyond even Malaysia's own territorial sea claims according to its own 1979 map, which Singapore has consistently rejected.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The inescapable conclusion is that the new Johor Bahru Port Limits transgress into what are indisputably Singapore Territorial Waters.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Since then, both sides have been engaged in intensive discussions to de-escalate the situation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have made reasonable progress so far, and I hope to make some joint announcements with my counterpart Foreign Minister Saifuddin Abdullah within the next one or two weeks.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng asked if the ongoing maritime dispute will affect the viability of our future Tuas Terminal.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Development works are proceeding as planned, and there will be no impact to access for ships calling at the terminal in the future.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I can assure Mr Ang that our security agencies will continue to be vigilant and safeguard the sovereignty and security of our territorial waters.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Now, let me move on to airspace issues.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I think it was Mr Pritam Singh who asked about Singapore's air navigation arrangements with our neighbours.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Those are the key words – safety and efficiency.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Air navigation arrangements, as Mr Pritam Singh knows, are complex, technical and operational matters which are under the jurisdiction of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO).

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: ICAO prioritises the safety and efficiency of civil aviation in all its policies, standards and recommended practices.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore's provision of air traffic services (ATS) for the region actually started way back in 1946, when ICAO allocated to Singapore the responsibility, the task for the provision of ATS in the Singapore Flight Information Region (FIR).

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: At the same time, ICAO also approved the arrangements under which Singapore would provide ATS over portions of southern Peninsular Malaysia, within the KL FIR.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The 1973 ICAO decision was a regional consensus, and struck a balance between the needs of both Singapore and Malaysia, and the international aviation community.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore and Malaysia concluded an agreement in 1974 to implement this ICAO decision.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Through these decades, Singapore has been providing ATS to the highest standards of safety and efficiency, in accordance with our responsibilities under international law, and ICAO's stipulated standards and practices.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Half of these 740,000 flights landed or departed from Changi Airport.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The other half consisted of overflights, many of which were, in fact, to and from other airports in the region.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The region's aviation sector has benefited greatly from all these arrangements.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This has been a win-win arrangement for the region, for our neighbours and for us.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are certainly willing to address their concerns, and let me also emphasise this.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore fully respects Malaysia's and Indonesia's sovereignty over their airspace.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: At the same time, discussions on air navigation arrangements must fundamentally be based on technical and operational considerations, for the purpose of ensuring the safety and efficiency of civil aviation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And any changes to these arrangements, if warranted, must be done properly, in accordance with the rules, the requirements and the decisions set out by ICAO.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Any such changes must further enhance safety and efficiency, and must benefit all airspace users.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And do not forget, stakeholders, such as airlines, who use this space, must also be consulted.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I agree with Mr Pritam Singh on the need to invest in technology so that Singapore remains the safest, the most reliable provider of air traffic services.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore has always recognised the edge that technology can bring, particularly in a highly technical field, such as ATS provision.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: CAAS has consistently invested in its air traffic management capabilities over many decades, focusing on three critical aspects: machine, man and method.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore's air traffic management systems are one of the most advanced in the world, and highly customised, incorporating cutting-edge technologies, such as space-based Automatic Dependent Surveillance (Broadcast) (ADS-B).

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Space-based ADS-B systems overcome the limitations of ground-based systems, which cannot be deployed over the vast expanse of sea to track aircraft.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: CAAS' air traffic controllers have been trained to a very high standard and are internationally recognised to be highly proficient, and they contribute extensively to setting global standards in ICAO and to industry organisations.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: CAAS' air traffic management processes and operating procedures are highly advanced and innovative whilst still maintaining fidelity to the highest safety standards.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: CAAS is a first-mover in developing and using advanced concepts in air traffic management.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: CAAS has pioneered the Distributed Multi-Nodal Air Traffic Flow Management (ATFM) network concept.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: ATFM basically helps to better manage traffic demand and capacity, particularly during times when there is an imbalance, and they do so by regulating flight arrival and departure times, taking into account live operational conditions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This project has succeeded in achieving fuel savings for airlines, reducing the period of time that aircraft spends in airborne holding patterns.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Now, even more Air Navigation Service Providers and airports around the region are keen to increase their involvement in the project.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our neighbours Malaysia and Indonesia are also participants in the project.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: CAAS has set up a new ATFM operations centre in the Singapore Air Traffic Control Centre to fully implement this concept in order to enhance Singapore’s air traffic service provision and contribution to the region.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore takes the air traffic management responsibilities that we have been entrusted with by ICAO very seriously.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will continue to invest in enhancing these capabilities and to discharge our responsibilities to the highest standards to achieve safety and efficiency and it will benefit the region and, indeed, the entire international aviation community.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng has asked about our bilateral discussions regarding Seletar Airport.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Chairman, I would now invite Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary to elaborate on the detailed plans for our land transport system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Chairman, our land transport network connects millions of Singaporeans every day to homes, jobs and schools.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is a shared space, an economic enabler and a social leveller.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As Minister Vivian Balakrishnan has noted, it is a maturing network, thanks to the efforts of leaders, planners and transport workers who have made this happen before us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: However, this maturing system brings with it a different set of challenges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Through our work on LTMP 2040, it is clear that tradeoffs between competing priorities are becoming more difficult to balance as we run up against tighter land, manpower and fiscal constraints.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, we have heard that Singaporeans value convenience and faster journeys.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: However, how do we provide this without compromising on safety and accessibility, especially for those with more diverse needs, such as the disabled?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Given our space constraints, how do we prioritise one mode of transport over another, knowing that this could result in slower speeds for some?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These are the realities we have to address for the next phase of development of our land transport system, and there are no easy answers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We must hold a long-term, clear-eyed view in managing these issues, and continue to enhance our land transport network to meet Singapore's and Singaporeans' growing needs, changing demographics and evolving aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We embarked on an extensive public consultation process to reach out to Singaporeans from all walks of life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Fourteen members from the public, private and people sectors joined the LTMP Advisory Panel to study the feedback received and to recommend the visions, targets and strategies for LTMP 2040.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Their ideas shaped the strategies and targets identified to improve our land transport system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We learned what Singaporeans value and want from our land transport system and we have set ourselves bold targets for 2040.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Public, active and shared transport is the only sustainable way forward with our land constraints.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Many active mobility services can also be shared but, specifically, we also want to include shared transport through taxis, private hire cars and shared vehicles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Some have asked whether this means that they will not benefit if their journeys today already take less than 20 or 45 minutes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These efforts to achieve 20-Minute Towns and 45-Minute City will benefit all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: LTA is now studying the specific initiatives to achieve these targets and will announce them in a few months' time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Even as they do so, it remains clear that a convenient, resilient and efficient public transport network will be central to us achieving this "20-Minute Towns and 45-Minute City" vision.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To achieve 20-Minute Towns, we will have to continue to improve connectivity within the towns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Apart from enhancing infrastructure to facilitate active mobility options for shorter, intra-town commutes, we are also conducting trials of on-demand public buses (ODPBs).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Melvin Yong asked for an update on the ongoing ODPB trial.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: While the technology is still evolving, the initial results are encouraging.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, 25% reduction in operated mileage, same journey times.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will continue to explore ways to improve the service by adapting these trial parameters and refining the ODPB algorithm.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will also monitor commuter feedback to assess how and if the trial can be expanded to include peak hours and weekends.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will help us to identify the key success factors for the ODPB concept, including adjustments to the way we roster our bus captains to ensure that they have sufficient rest.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In time to come, we can also explore virtual bus stops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But this will require us to strike a careful balance between safety and convenience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will also study the extent to which ODPBs can improve first- and last-mile connectivity to allow even more Singaporeans to benefit, regardless of their proximity to an MRT station.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Such dynamically routed bus services have the potential to reduce travelling and waiting times for intra-town journeys and allow commuters to enjoy more seamless commutes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To achieve a 45-Minute City, I agree with Mr Ang Wei Neng that rail must continue to be the backbone of our public transport network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Even as we pursue our ambitions, I am happy to report that we are on track to achieve the targets set in our last LTMP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The announcement of the Jurong Region Line in 2018 and the first phase of the Cross Island Line (CRL) earlier this year puts us yet another step closer to having eight in 10 households within a 10-minute walk from a train station.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This was the previous LTMP target to achieve in 2030, 10 years before the outcomes that we are hoping for in LTMP 2040.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will continue to review and expand our rail network where there is sufficient ridership.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Hume station was originally designed as a shell station on DTL2 as the pace of developments and ridership growth in the area did not warrant it opening with the other DTL2 stations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mayor Low Yen Ling has worked hard on behalf of her residents, and she has worked with our public sector agencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: She has highlighted and advocated for the potential of the area and the needs of her residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have worked closely with her and her community leaders to see how we can improve the commuting experience for residents in the new estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Since then, these new development plans have been made, partly because of the advocacy and the engagement by Mayor Low Yen Ling and her community leaders for the redevelopment of the Rail Corridor and the transformation of the nearby Bukit Timah Fire Station into a Gateway Node for the surrounding nature and heritage attractions and other developments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Likewise, further addition of new bus services in Bukit Gombak will depend on the pace of development and ridership growth in the area.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are also studying other rail projects beyond 2030 that will bring us closer to the “45-Minute City”.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These will be announced when the LTMP is launched in a few months.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As Sitoh Yih Pin has pointed out, it is important that we continue to exercise financial prudence as we develop our land transport network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In deciding which areas to extend our rail network to, we will have to balance between managing costs and benefiting the most number of Singaporeans possible, taking into account the characteristics of each area.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As an example, I would like to address the suggestion by Mr Arasu Duraisamy that we study the feasibility of a new MRT line to Tuas South and Jurong Island.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For Tuas South, the area is still in the initial stages of development and there is not enough ridership in the near to medium term to support an MRT line.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Nevertheless, we have taken steps to improve bus connectivity to the Tuas South area.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: With the opening of the Tuas West Extension in June 2017, LTA launched two new public bus services in the Tuas South area, that is, services 247 and 248.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: When the Jurong Region Line (JRL) and Cross Island Line are completed, workers in Tuas South will benefit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As for Jurong Island, there are no plans to extend the MRT onto the island itself.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: However, workers will benefit from the future Jurong Pier Station, which is located only a short distance away from Jurong Island Checkpoint.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, if we were to put a station on Jurong Island itself, it is unlikely to create any added convenience or time savings because the workers would still have to go through the Checkpoint security and transfer to an onward last-mile shuttle to their final destination, given how spread out the developments are on the island.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, we will have to balance the effectiveness of such a solution and the costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Chairman, we cannot achieve our vision of 20-Minute Towns and a 45-Minute City through infrastructure developments alone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our public transport system is built to support peak travel demand during the short two-hour window on weekday mornings and evenings, as many Singaporeans living all over the island commute to jobs in the city centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We need to optimise the distribution of jobs and housing across the island.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will reduce travel times as more people live closer to their workplace.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is, in fact, another way of redistributing peak travel demand and make better use of transport infrastructure, as noted by Assoc Prof Walter Theseira.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These will be well connected by Transit Priority Corridors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Taken altogether, the redistribution, these Transit Priority Corridors, the work that we are already doing on the MRT lines will shorten our daily commutes to work and play and take us closer to our vision of 20-Minute Towns and a 45-Minute City.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The second key recommendation by the Advisory Panel is to build a more Inclusive Transport System.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Through the LTMP public consultation process, Singaporeans have expressed their desire for a land transport system which is inclusive and welcoming to all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This means a culture where commuters look out for one another, especially those who are more in need.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Singaporeans acknowledged that achieving this gracious commuting culture is a shared responsibility between the Government, transport operators, transport workers and commuters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I am heartened that Singaporeans are willing to play their part, and my colleague Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey Yam Keng will later elaborate on strategies to make our land transport system a more inclusive and friendly space for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These planned infrastructural enhancements and the inclusion strategies will complement efforts towards the Panel's third key recommendation on Healthy Lives and Safer Journeys.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: A comprehensive suite of public, active and shared transport options will reduce our reliance on privately-owned vehicles and contribute towards a healthier environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will complement ongoing initiatives by different Ministries to improve the health of Singapore and Singaporeans, including through the reduction of vehicle emissions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, we work with the Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources on the Vehicular Emissions Scheme and the Early Turnover Scheme to encourage owners to use cleaner vehicles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The electric car-sharing programme, jointly supported by LTA and the Economic Development Board, is another example.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Government will also take the lead in building a cleaner transport system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I am pleased to announce that key industry players in the P2P sector are also following the Government's lead.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is the first time that we have an industry-led target for LTMP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Apart from a healthier environment, we will continue to encourage active mobility as a way to meet Singaporeans' aspirations for a healthier life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Supporting this will require us to change the way we plan towns, to make active modes of transport more convenient.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Senior Minister of State Lam Pin Min will elaborate further on some of the initiatives planned to encourage more commuters to incorporate healthier modes of transport into their daily routines.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: While we plan to improve speeds and convenience, I agree with Miss Cheng Li Hui that safety cannot be compromised.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our bus safety record has improved over the past year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But every life lost on our roads or paths is one too many.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We must work towards reducing land transport fatalities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To do this, we will introduce more pedestrian-friendly features, such as Silver Zones, to reduce vehicular speeds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Third, we are exploring enhanced safety management systems, such as anti-fatigue, collision warning and blindspot warning systems, to aid our bus captains.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These will provide audio cues or vibrations to keep the driver alert, and they are already a standard requirement for our public buses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Chairman, many of our LTMP 2040 strategies rely on technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Technological innovations in recent years have increased mobility options for commuters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There are also better journey-planning applications, including LTA's MyTransport.SG mobile app, to help commuters plan multi-modal journeys.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This, in turn, has improved the accessibility and utilisation of public transport.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have also used technology to make our commutes easier, such as through Account-based Ticketing (ABT).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Since March 2017, LTA has partnered MasterCard to test the use of contactless bankcards on public transport under the ABT initiative.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The pilot was successful and LTA is now working with MasterCard and Visa on the full launch of ABT under the branding of "SimplyGo".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Starting April 2019, all MasterCard users with compatible contactless cards or mobile phones can use these on our buses and trains.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We plan for Visa to be used on public transport later this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: With "SimplyGo", commuters will have the option of carrying one less card for transport, or maybe no cards if they use their mobile phones, and not having to do card top-ups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: AVs are another area which can allow us to reinvent how land transport is provided, such as dynamically routed services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: AVs will also help us to create new job opportunities in the transport sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: ST Engineering Land Systems is conducting a trial of autonomous buses and partnering SBST to deploy a few of its bus captains as safety operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: While the widespread deployment of AVs is still years away, such trials give us an early sense of the requirements for the new job roles that will be created.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I agree with Assoc Prof Walter Theseira that our regulatory frameworks must also be flexible enough to guide the flow of technology without constricting it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We must strike a balance between protecting the public interest, achieving our broader transport policy objectives, allowing innovations to thrive, meeting the needs of commuters and creating jobs for transport workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We need to be clear about what, why and how we want to regulate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: How we have evolved our planned regulatory framework for the P2P sector is a good example.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The rapid growth of ride-hailing applications has disrupted the P2P sector in many cities, leading to strikes, driver unhappiness and commuter inconvenience around the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Here in Singapore, we have been relatively fortunate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Commuter satisfaction with P2P services continues to remain high.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Such a positive outcome is only possible with responsible operators, sensible commuters, safe drivers and sound policy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In particular, the National Taxi Association (NTA) and the National Private Hire Vehicles Association (NPHVA) have played important roles in helping our drivers adjust to technological transformation in the P2P space.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are in the process of reviewing our regulatory approach for the P2P sector to ensure that commuters can continue to benefit from a robust and safe P2P space.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Ang Hin Kee and Mr Ang Wei Neng spoke about the ongoing P2P review.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We intend to introduce a new licensing process for all P2P operators focusing on three key areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The majority of P2P drivers will then be free to choose which operators to drive for, thus ensuring that the P2P industry continues to be a viable and sustainable sector to make a living in.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Second, we will focus on commuter safety, where all P2P operators will have to play their part to keep commuters and drivers safe.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Third, we will minimise business and regulatory costs for operators and drivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Part of this involves streamlining, where appropriate, the regulatory differences between street-hail and ride-hail services, such as the taxi availability services that Mr Ang Wei Neng has raised.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: More details will be made available later this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These principles will lay the ground for a safe, open and contestable P2P sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: New players and different business models will be able to enter and start providing P2P solutions for our commuters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng and Mr Ang Hin Kee had made suggestions about market size and P2P fares, and we will study their feedback.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our intention is not to regulate every single aspect of the P2P market, but to allow market forces to shape some of these more efficiently and to let competition drive innovation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Ultimately, commuters and drivers will be able to benefit from better services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will help us to achieve our 20-Minute Towns and 45-Minute City vision.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As Mr Ang Hin Kee and Mr Ang Wei Neng are aware, our review has been happening in consultation with the industry, as well as the Labour Movement, represented by NTA and NPHVA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As we enter the final stages of our review, we will continue to work closely with our tripartite stakeholders to manage disruptions, consider the feedback received, keep in mind the need to protect commuter interests and also taking into account suggestions, such as Mr Ang Hin Kee's, to protect driver interests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will do so while streamlining regulations and managing business costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Together, these will provide platforms for LTA, drivers and operators to discuss strategic issues concerning the P2P sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We recently completed our public consultation exercise on 21 February.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Members of the public have expressed strong support for the policies that we intend to roll out as part of the new regulatory framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We agree with and will respond to the call for a more inclusive P2P sector and will work closely with the industry on this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: More details will be provided in the coming months.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Chairman, our land transport sector will continue to create opportunities for Singaporean workers and businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Melvin Yong asked about efforts to support public transport workers and meeting future challenges in the land transport sector, including the development and deployment of AVs in future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will continue to work with unions and industry partners to help workers respond to these emerging technologies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In February 2018, we launched the Land Transport ITM.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Under this ITM, the Government is working closely with the unions and operators to upskill our workers to equip them with the capabilities to do their jobs efficiently and effectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is being done through our Institutes of Higher Learning, as well as through the Singapore Bus Academy and Singapore Rail Academy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have also established the ITM Tripartite Steering Committee co-chaired by NTWU and LTA to identify interventions to help workers respond to these emerging technologies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This cooperation between company management and unions is critical to developing a future-ready workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I agree with Mr Ang Wei Neng that developing local capabilities is vital to ensuring industry resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: However, offset conditions, such as the transfer of technology, which are prohibited under our international obligations, are not the only way to achieve this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Many of our local companies are already partnering LTA on civil construction projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Hock Lian Seng and Lum Chang Building Contractors are two such companies which initially partnered other international contractors and made use of these opportunities to grow their experience and capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Today, they take on complex rail and road infrastructure projects on their own.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They started growing their rail capabilities by performing works for the North-South and East-West Lines in the 1980s.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And now they go on to secure contracts overseas and are a major supplier of Passenger Information Systems for railways in several countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Looking ahead, there will be more such opportunities, and we look forward to the continued involvement of local businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is not just about the shared space or being a social leveller that the public transport system is.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is not simply about building the roads or buying the buses or the trains or building new types of land transport systems.
