speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: During the debate, several Members shared about the frustrations of pedestrians when they encounter irresponsible riders.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Stories were told about pedestrians who were injured by reckless riders of PMDs or cyclists and about the elderly or young children who had close shaves with these riders.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Notwithstanding the various measures taken by LTA enforcement officers, I still receive many complaints about reckless and dangerous behaviour of cyclists and users of PMDs.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Sadly, many cyclists still behave irresponsibly even though they are cycling in areas where there are many pedestrians, some of whom are elderly and some of whom are young children.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The most challenging area is where there are food delivery companies.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In the areas surrounding the food delivery companies, the PMD riders and the cyclists ride in a reckless and unsafe manner as they rush to deliver their food to the customers.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The Ride Safe lessons conducted currently only reach out to those riders who are converted and who are convinced about the need for safety.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: For those who do not care about safety or the need to be considerate to other road users, they do not bother to attend such safety lessons.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Will there be a step-up in enforcement against reckless and inconsiderate riders?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: How can an enforcement officer determine the speed of the PMD or bicycle?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: How about the mandatory use of helmets by cyclists on roads?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Will the cyclist riding along a small road from his home to the bus stop or to the market be summoned if he does not put on a helmet?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Would these rules also apply to the foreign workers riding from their dormitory to their workplace?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I urge the Minister to expedite the steps to ensure that all road users, including pedestrians, PMD users and cyclists can have a safer journey when using footpaths and the roads.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister share some updated statistics for 2018?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: How many such accidents were serious enough that someone was sent to hospital?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I understand the AMAP’s preference to prioritise reduction of accidents.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But accidents will happen, and some of them will be so serious that they require large, hefty medical fees.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Without insurance, the perpetrator or victim will have trouble paying off these fees.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It is a double blow when the accident victim rides as part of his work and he can no longer do so because he is injured, or his vehicle is damaged.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: For a start, perhaps let us make it mandatory for all employers who rely on their employees to use PMDs for work purposes.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The Government can work with insurance companies to help companies get a more affordable deal.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I know most e-scooters will not get into accidents.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But the same can be said for car drivers, and motor insurance is still mandatory.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And just like for cars, we need constant enforcement to make sure people stay within the rules.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Residents have been giving feedback that, during morning peak hours, there are a lot of PMDs, e-scooters, bicycles zooming along covered linkways leading to the MRT station.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister share how much LTA has stepped up enforcement, and how LTA decides how much enforcement they should do?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Next, to prevent unnecessary accidents in housing estates, it would be prudent to ban bicycles and PMDs at areas which are crowded or known to be accident-prone.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The best organisation to do so would be the Town Council, which receives a lot of feedback on such issues.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Last, but not least, I wish my favourite Minister a speedy recovery.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Mr Chairman, I certainly agree with the comments the hon Mr Lim Biow Chuan just delivered.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: However, even before my Parliamentary Question (PQ) was answered, prospective operator Beam announced in October that it planned to roll out its shared PMD services within the next few weeks.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: In December 2018, I chanced upon a few PMDs with the familiar green logo of Grab displayed and parked outside a shophouse along Jalan Sultan.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I was surprised to see this, given the answer to my PQ just a month before.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I enquired with LTA and LTA confirmed that Grab was not allowed to operate on public land without a licence from LTA and they said they were investigating operators who were operating without a licence.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I have also seen PMDs belonging to other operators being used on public lands.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: The fact that these operators have been operating their PMDs in public without a licence is disconcerting.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: If operators behave in this way without a proper licence, how can we have confidence in such companies toeing the line after they receive a licence?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: We should also remember Grab’s reaction to the Competition Commission’s findings on its acquisition of Uber.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: In his reply to my PQ, Senior Minister of State Lam Pin Min set out some of the conditions which would be imposed on the shared PMD operators upon issuance of their licence.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I agree with those conditions but, notwithstanding these conditions, my reservations regarding the introduction of commercial shared PMD services have remained.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: It has been difficult enough to ensure that all PMD owners adhere to new rules for safe use of PMDs and to be considerate to other footpath users.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: We are not out of the woods yet.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Would it not exacerbate the present situation if we have a new category of users, namely, hirers?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Hirers are likely to take less ownership of the need to ride responsibly and considerately compared to owners since they are not the owners.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Even if conditions are imposed on the operators, there is a limit as to what operators can do to ensure that correct use of PMDs is adopted by all users.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: While it is good to require operators to have insurance for all users, which may be helpful when there is an accident leading to a personal injury or property damage claim, this does not stop inconsiderate or unlawful behavior and, certainly, near misses.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: The biggest challenge is still of getting existing PMD owners and users to use the PMDs in accordance with the law and in a safe and considerate manner.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: What more can we expect from hitherto non-PMD users, namely, hirers?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Already, I have seen quite a number of tourists or overseas visitors on the illegally operated PMDs, some of them even riding on the roads.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: What does LTA expect the operators to do to ensure that users will ride considerately and according to the regulations?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Make them mug up all the rules before scooting off?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Mr Chairman, the Land Transport Masterplan 2040 vision of a car-lite Singapore is an ambitious and enticing one.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: To achieve these ambitious targets not only requires new infrastructure but also changes in lifestyle and commuting habits.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: To these ends, I would like to inquire how we are progressing in expanding pedestrian walkways to accommodate pedestrians and PMD users.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: And since the implementation of active mobility rules on 1 February 2019, how has enforcement kept up to ensure that PMD users are safety conscious and responsible users of public paths?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Education is also an important part of the equation.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How are we working with the community to disseminate good and safe etiquette on shared paths?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: What guidelines are in place for PMDs and how do we ensure that the current stock of PMDs in the market are safe for PMD users and the community around them?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: Mr Chairman, the licence application period for PMD sharing services has just ended earlier this month.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: If so, how will the Ministry be requiring that these operators place a security deposit or performance bond?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: In addition, the usage of PMDs in the hands of the young and inexperienced riders can be potentially hazardous to both the path users and themselves.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: Therefore, I would like to ask the Minister if there will be a mandatory age requirement for users to operate PMDs as age can be a form of indication on users' abilities to comprehend rules and operate PMDs safely.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
text: One design just makes it clear these are reserved seats with prominent "Reserved Seating" stickers being pasted on the seats themselves as well as above the seats.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Mr Chairman, Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary touched on the infrastructure improvements we have implemented to improve public transport and P2P connectivity.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: My speech will focus on making active mobility viable for shorter journeys and first-and-last-mile connections to transport nodes, while allowing Singaporeans to meet their aspirations for healthy living.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: During the recent public engagements for LTMP 2040, some participants I spoke to mentioned that they use their daily commute to squeeze in a little bit of exercise by walking and cycling.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: They wanted to see more options for walking and cycling between destinations.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Others expressed hopes for safer path-sharing and more harmonious interactions among path users.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We support these aspirations by Singaporeans and will enhance our transport system to facilitate active and healthy lifestyles and to ensure safety for all.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: To help more Singaporeans embrace active mobility, we will continue to enhance active mobility accessibility, while inculcating a safe and gracious path-sharing culture to address pedestrians' concerns with path-sharing.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: First, we are expanding active mobility options through building more cycling infrastructure.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA will also build the Geylang-City and Queenstown-City inter-town cycling routes.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: When completed in 2020, they will connect cyclists and PMD users directly from their homes to the city.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With the increased popularity of active mobility, Singaporeans have expressed concerns about safety on paths shared by pedestrians and PMD users.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As Mr Lim Biow Chuan and Ms Sun Xueling have pointed out, active mobility accidents have increased due to the increased use of bicycles and PMDs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: To stem this worrying trend, AMAP conducted a review of active mobility rules in 2018.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In January, we started the registration regime for e-scooters to deter reckless riding behaviour and facilitate enforcement efforts in tracking down errant riders.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We also reduced the speed limit on footpaths from 15 km/h to 10 km/h in February this year.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: To address Mr Lim Biow Chuan's query, a slower speed gives active mobility users and pedestrians more time to react to unforeseen circumstances and reduces the risk of severe injuries should accidents occur.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Last year, AMAP recommended against mandating third-party liability insurance so as to accommodate the diversity of active mobility device users and keep active mobility affordable.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Nonetheless, we echo Er Dr Lee Bee Wah's sentiments on the importance of third-party liability insurance and strongly encourage users to insure themselves against third-party claims.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: To this end, LTA and AMAP have engaged the insurance industry and employers of large groups of active mobility users, such as food delivery companies, to spur the provision of insurance coverage.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Similarly, we will require PMD-sharing licensees to procure and maintain third-party liability insurance.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah also asked that Town Councils be allowed to ban bicycles and PMDs for pedestrian safety.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The Active Mobility Act allows pedestrians, cyclists and PMD users to use footpaths as they are crucial for connectivity.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: It is important that the same rules are applied consistently to all footpaths so that users will not be confused with different rules at different areas.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will continue to review our regulations to ensure the safety of all path users and will take the suggestions into account for the next review.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: To safeguard pedestrian safety, we will consider infrastructural improvements where necessary, such as pedestrian priority zones which employ "SLOW" markings, speed regulating strips and signages to alert cyclists and riders to slow down and look out for pedestrians.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I fully agree with Miss Cheng Li Hui, Ms Sun Xueling, Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and Mr Lim Biow Chuan on the need for stronger enforcement to deter reckless riding behaviour.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA's team of Active Mobility Enforcement Officers has been carrying out regular checks at hotspots, using speed guns and weighing scales to enforce speed limit and device weight requirements.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: To complement its existing enforcement efforts, LTA will implement a trial later this year to place closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras at hotspots for better detection of active mobility offences.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As Mr Lim Biow Chuan has rightly pointed out, we also need to educate users on responsible behaviour.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We have pressed on with the Safe Riding Programme, which educates active mobility device users on safe riding practices and proper use of active mobility infrastructure.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In its first year, 39,000 participants from schools, companies and the community completed the programme.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will continue to offer the programme at a fully subsidised rate until the end of 2019, so that more will be able to participate.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA has also worked with MOM and Traffic Police to issue a joint circular to food delivery companies to encourage food delivery riders to ride safely and provide avenues for members of the public to report unsafe riding.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I also agree with Ms Sun Xueling on the need to introduce guidelines to improve the safety of PMDs and reduce fire risks.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We have strongly advised PMD users to purchase PMDs from reputable sources, observe fire safety standards and avoid overcharging PMD batteries or modifying their PMDs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: However, there are some places where this is not possible.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will, therefore, need to strive for an ethos of gracious path-sharing where cyclists, PMD users and pedestrians look out for one another's safety.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Ground-up initiatives, such as the Active Mobility Patrol (AMP) scheme, will play a crucial role in harnessing the community to promote harmonious path-sharing behaviour.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We now have more than 1,000 volunteers conducting patrols and organising outreach activities in their communities to educate cyclists and PMD users on how they should adjust their behaviour to accommodate the needs of fellow path-users.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In recent years, operators offering active mobility device-sharing services have emerged.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: While it offers Singaporeans better access to active mobility devices at cheap prices, it also comes with its own share of challenges.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The regime regulates the maximum fleet size for each licensee based on responsible operator behaviour, and aligns fleet growth with parking provisions and consumer needs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In January this year, we introduced measures to ensure that users park responsibly, such as the quick response (QR) code parking system, and requiring operators to ban recalcitrant users from device-sharing services.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With these efforts, we have made great strides in bringing the indiscriminate parking situation under control.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The number of shared bicycle trips ending outside a designated parking location has been declining steadily, and we will continue to work with operators to reduce indiscriminate parking.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Miss Cheng Li Hui asked about what we have learnt from the oBike incident.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: OBike's sudden exit preceded our licensing regime and deeply inconvenienced many Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The licensing regime will help to address some of the disamenities caused by oBike's exit.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For example, when oBike exited, it was difficult to locate the individual bicycles left behind which did not have location-tracking features.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Under our licensing regime, licensees are required to install location tracking devices on their bicycles and prepare plans to remove their bicycles in a timely manner should they exit the market.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This year, we opened a second round of licence applications for bicycle-sharing services on 4 January.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This allows new operators to enter the market and gives responsible licensees that are able to manage their fleets effectively the opportunity to grow their fleets.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Miss Cheng Li Hui asked if PMD-sharing licensees will require users to put up deposits.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Based on the licence applications we have received, no PMD-sharing licence applicant intends to require user deposits.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Mr Dennis Tan and Miss Cheng Li Hui expressed concern over the operations of PMD-sharing services, and the impact of allowing PMD-sharing services at this time.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This gives LTA time to assess sandbox licensees’ ability to comply with regulatory requirements, before granting them a larger fleet size under a full licence.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA may revoke the licence of non-compliant sandbox licensees during the licence period.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: PMD-sharing licensees will be subjected to PMD-specific safety requirements.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: These include ensuring that shared PMDs are charged only by suitable personnel in proper environments and requiring shared PMDs to be certified to the UL2272 standard.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: PMD-sharing licensees will also be required to procure and maintain third-party liability insurance, and to have identification stickers and tracking devices installed on devices to facilitate enforcement.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I am confident that our licensing approach and regulatory requirements will allow us to start on the right footing for PMD-sharing services.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Mr Chairman, we will continue to support Singaporeans’ aspirations for healthier lifestyles and safer journeys.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As active mobility becomes more popular, we will continue to promote a safe path-sharing culture and ensure that device-sharing operators provide their services in a safe and responsible manner.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, during the Land Transport Master Plan 2040 public engagement, many Singaporeans came forward to share their aspirations and concerns.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We hear them and we will plan for a future-ready land transport system.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Yee Chia Hsing would be pleased to know that we are aspiring towards a more inclusive land transport system, which caters to the diverse mobility needs of all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The LTMP Advisory Panel recommended three strategies to help us achieve this.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Last year, we completed a five-year programme to add 200 km of sheltered walkways to make walking to our public transport nodes more convenient and pleasant.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Ms Low Yen Ling requested for sheltered walkways.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: LTA will continue to provide the same extent of sheltered walkway connectivity between all public transport nodes and developments, whenever new MRT lines or developments are built.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We must be careful in considering other locations to ensure that limited resources are focused on areas which can benefit more people.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will continue to do more for our seniors and take steps to enhance road safety for them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We are building another 20 Silver Zones by 2020 at areas, including Ang Mo Kio Avenue 10, Potong Pasir Avenue 1 and Tampines Street 81.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We are on track to achieve our target of 50 Silver Zones by 2023.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As LTA continues to work with the community on design of these identified locations, we are also adopting innovative solutions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In December 2018, LTA tested three-dimensional traffic calming markings along Whampoa Drive to slow down traffic.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: LTA has also installed light emitting diode (LED) road studs at zebra crossings to alert motorists of pedestrians at night.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I urge all motorists to slow down and be even more alert to look out for pedestrians when approaching these areas.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Besides infrastructure enhancements, we also need to have a robust vehicle homologation regime.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This refers to LTA’s process to ensure that new vehicle models meet all technical and safety requirements before they can be used on our roads.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: During last week’s Budget Debate, Mr Ang Wei Neng said that the process takes eight weeks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I checked and I am glad to find that this is not correct.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Even if we include the time to clarify an incomplete application, the average total time taken was five weeks in 2018.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The regime is aligned with internationally recognised standards, such as the UN Economic Commission for Europe Regulations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: LTA will continue to engage industry stakeholders to streamline the process to reduce business costs, while ensuring safety.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Besides physical accessibility, we also want to make information, such as service number and bus stop destination, more accessible to commuters with special needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In January 2019, LTA started a trial on Mobility Assistance for the Visually Impaired and Special Users mobile app.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This provides audio announcements both on the bus and at the bus stop to help bus commuters with special needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The trial started with three buses on Service 139, which serves the Enabling Village.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These three buses will subsequently be redeployed in May 2019 to Service 141, which serves the Singapore Association of the Visually Handicapped.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This will help us to study the feasibility of such assistive technologies on more public bus services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Last year, the Government received recommendations from the Family Friendly Transport Advisory Panel.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, LTA started a one-year trial for the stroller restraint system on Service 69 in June 2017.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We received positive feedback and will progressively install the system on all buses by 2020.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: LTA will be conducting a pilot on one rail line, to designate priority cabins for vulnerable commuters, such as seniors, persons with disabilities and families with young children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These cabins will be located near the station lifts where possible.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Beyond mass public transport, we will also make P2P transport more accessible by designing all new taxi stands to be barrier-free.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, our second strategy is to develop the capabilities of our public transport workers as they make important contributions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I agree with Mr Melvin Yong that a first-class transport system needs a first-class transport workforce.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Land transport workers work hard daily to bring millions of Singaporeans safely to their destinations and they also offer assistance regularly for those in need to make their journeys easier.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Bus captains start their day as early as 4.00 am and rail technicians work throughout the night to carry out maintenance works.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Public Transport Workers’ Appreciation Day was launched in 2017.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Last year, the event was held at the Istana for the very first time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This emphasises the important contributions by our public transport workers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, an inclusive land transport system requires everyone to play their part.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Government will continue to invest in inclusive infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The public transport workers also play an important role to support more vulnerable commuters.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Lastly, commuters must contribute in creating a safe community space, fostering positive social norms and a caring commuting culture.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This is the third strategy recommended by the LTMP Advisory Panel.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: LTA began Graciousness Campaigns for public transport in 2009, to promote simple acts of thoughtful behaviour, such as giving up seats and queueing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: LTA has been progressively replacing the reserved seat stickers on trains with new stickers featuring the Thoughtful Character, Stand-Up Stacey.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: LTA's perception study showed that the new stickers have helped to sustain interest in terms of commuters giving up their seats.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Indeed, Singaporeans are willing to go the extra mile to help fellow commuters.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: At the Heart Zones at Jurong East, Novena and Outram Park MRT stations, the community readily come forward to help patients who need assistance to get to the nearby hospitals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We want to encourage a culture where small caring gestures can make a difference.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Some of my Parliamentary colleagues told me they are interested to offer needy residents credits to top up their fare cards, very much like how the National Trades Union Congress FairPrice vouchers are used to help them purchase daily necessities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, please allow me a few more minutes to complete the last part of my speech in Mandarin.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: (In Mandarin):   Building a safe and inclusive land transport system requires everyone − the Government, transport workers and commuters – to play their part.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Infrastructure and campaigns alone are not enough to build a more gracious society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For a sustained change in behaviour, we need commuters to look out for one another.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I encourage Singaporeans to be positive influences to others in their daily lives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We can do so by caring for fellow commuters, pedestrians and transport workers when we use public transport, footpaths or roads.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Put others before yourself, lend a hand to those who need help.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, even if you are not on a "reserved seat", you can still give up your seat to those who need it more than you do.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: When on the road, drive safely and look out for pedestrians.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Slow down at all areas, not just at Silver Zones.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Together, I believe we can create a safe and inclusive land transport system where every journey can be more comfortable, heart-warming and pleasant.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Lastly, I hope to encourage all of us towards this vision with this short poem: "Commuting in Singapore Moving together as one Without caring for others around you It will be a difficult journey Show that you care And we will all feel the warmth Be it driving, riding or walking We can all be safe and happy!"

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Mr Chairman, I have clarifications for Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary and for Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey Yam Keng.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: During my cut on "20-minute Town and 40-minute City", I have asked how many households today are staying within a 10-minute walk of an MRT station and how many current trips today to city are taking less than 45 minutes so that we can have a benchmark, compared to our Vision in 2040.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: I hope the Senior Minister of State can also enlighten us whether MOT has given up hope to persuade Government agencies and companies to have staggered working hours so as to smoothen out the traffic during peak hours.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: For Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey Yam Keng, I am glad that LTA has made the clarification on homologations, but this is only one example that I quoted for agencies to look at how to cut red tape.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: In fact, the experience on the ground is actually quite different.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Mr Ang Wei Neng for the question.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: He asked how many households are within a 10-minute walk to an MRT station today.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The second point the Member asked about staggered working hours, yes, LTA and MOT, we will try our best to encourage people to adopt staggered working hours.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It will be another strategy to help smoothen out the load and the demand on our public transport system.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In response to the Member's speech last week, perhaps he was just quoting the specific example.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: But LTA is committed to streamlining homologation regulations and, not just that, but also in all processes so that we can provide better services to the public.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to express my heartfelt gratitude to Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary, in particular, Minister Khaw Boon Wan and as well as to MOT, LTA for the good news of Hume MRT station.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Throughout the years, Minister Khaw Boon Wan and his team have been very patient in listening to our transport requests and we are very grateful for this good news.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In Gombak, Hillview and Hume, we stand ready towards the LTA and MOT with regard to the building of Hume MRT station.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I have one clarification for Senior Minister of State Dr Janil Puthucheary: is there a chance that the Hume MRT station can be completed before 2025, please?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Mayor Low Yen Ling for the question.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are in this position today because Mayor Low and her grassroots leaders have worked hard with our agencies, as well as with MND and the various agencies, to look into how development can be brought into that area and new facilities can be created, new opportunities can begin, as a result of which, we can now justify the ridership for Hume MRT station going forward.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, we do need some time to pass for the developments, justifying the opening of Hume MRT station to occur.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: On top of that, it is not just that we have to open Hume station, but we have to build Hume station, and that would take some time.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There is going to be architectural works, earthworks, ventilation shafts, and we have to do so together with the other developments around the area so that we do not obstruct some of the new things that are coming up.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, we will try our best, but I am pleased to repeat that we will be opening Hume station by 2025.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: When is the cycling path going to be completed?

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: Is the cycling path going to be a separate standalone cycling path away from the existing footpaths?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Mr Chairman, I just want to thank Dr Teo Ho Pin for that clarification.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy
text: I have a question for Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy
text: In his reply, he mentioned that since the Tuas South station would still be in its development phase and the anticipated ridership would be low, could he then explain to me what is the rationale when we are about to spend a quarter of a million dollars to build the Founders Memorial station and there are no projected numbers on that particular station?

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy
text: What is the development process that is going to go around that particular station?

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy
text: His reply was that Tuas South station would still be in the development phase.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy
text: I anticipate that Founders Memorial station would also still be in the development phase.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy
text: They are both in that particularly, but the Senior Minister of State has also earlier projected to build a station there.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy
text: So, could the Senior Minister of State then explain to me the rationale why he could not look at a line down to Tuas South?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Mr Chairman, it is not that everything has to be developed before we bring in an MRT line or a transport service, but it is the confidence around the ridership.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, there is no single development or facility that will say this is the right thing to do or this is the wrong thing to do.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We have to look at the total expected demand.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: For Tuas South, yes, in the long term, there may be a very different demand picture from what we expect today.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But on the basis of what we are currently projecting, it is not something that we can justify at this point in time in the medium term.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: One is for Senior Minister of State Lam Pin Min on air transport.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: I notice that we are making a lot of effort to have air agreements in order for us to have more air traffic.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: The second clarification is for Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: I am just wondering whether LTA or MOT will assist the industry to form an association because, right now, the operators are all individuals.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: So, when they come for the meetings, they come as individuals, rather than a collective association.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: So, sometimes, the voices can be very disparate and they do not quite have a common position on whether the industry operators want to bring to the table to negotiate.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to thank Mr Ang Hin Kee for his clarification.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In fact, we have received similar feedback from Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, and I do empathise with the disamenities with regard to noise pollution for residents who are staying in the vicinity of Seletar Airport.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: CAAS is mindful of the noise generated by overflying aircraft and we have been reviewing and adopting best practices in noise abatement measures according to international standards.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: To the extent possible, CAAS will direct aircraft to land away from and take off towards directions to minimise flying over residential areas.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This will, hopefully, reduce the amount of noise disturbances.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: However, for safety reasons, aircraft need to land and take off into the wind and, depending on the prevailing wind conditions, it is sometimes unavoidable for aircraft to overfly residential areas, especially those in the Yishun and Yio Chu Kang areas.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: At the same time, CAAS also disallows older jet aircraft that do not meet international standards on aircraft noise certification from flying into Singapore.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Jet aircraft which operate to Seletar Airport are generally newer and quieter ones.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This will hopefully reduce the amount of noise pollution in the evening and at night.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Mr Chairman, I have to answer Mr Ang Hin Kee's question about the private hire vehicle drivers.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In the first part, Mr Ang Hin Kee asked about the operators forming an association because the drivers are already part of NPHVA.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Well, certainly, we can engage with the operators and the business to do this.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Potentially, we have a number of businesses that can get involved with the P2P space.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Some would be traditional taxi companies and transport operators; some would be the very new mobility operators that we have seen coming to Singapore.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But potentially, even tech companies could get into it.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, it is not a very clear industry as to who would be a partner.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will engage with them all, and if there is a need to form an association, we may have to look for some assistance to chair the committee and so forth, but we will definitely be engaging Mr Ang Hin Kee to help us engage in this process.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will have to look and see what will be the reasonable thing to do.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: The first question is for Minister Vivian Balakrishnan.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: In the event of the withdrawal of air traffic services by Singapore over south Johor or the Riau Islands, may I ask the Minister what is his view on how it would affect Changi Airport as an air hub, as well as its future development?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: My second question goes to Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary who said that the bus and taxi operators are committed to using cleaner technology by 2040, if I hear him correctly.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: So, may I ask the Senior Minister of State: since the bus and taxi operators are already so committed, is there really still a need to use diesel tax to, in the words of Minister Heng Swee Keat, "nudge these operators towards cleaner and more sustainable alternatives"?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: My third and fourth questions go to Senior Minister of State Lam Pin Min.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: My clarification is: will the errant behaviour of the customer hirers of the shared PMD operators be taken into account when the LTA assesses the relevant operators complying with the sandbox licence conditions, or in respect of the specific hirers' eligibility to continue hiring e-scooters with any of the commercial operators?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: When can we expect this to be introduced in our statutes?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As I explained just now, I want to clearly differentiate between sovereignty and airspace, and the responsibility for the provision of air traffic services.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, let us be very clear that we are not arguing about sovereignty.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As I also explained earlier, there is a long history as to why and how Singapore provides these air traffic services.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I have also emphasised that the main objective, regardless of who is performing, is the safety and efficiency of civil aviation.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, we are a long way from the hypothetical scenario which the Member has posited.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I would say this, that Changi Airport is one of the world's busiest airports, and certainly in our immediate region, this is the focal point on which so many flights traversed.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, our objectives in all our ongoing discussions with our neighbours are to make sure that safety and efficiency are not compromised.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The other salient factor is this: technology is also improving and it will help improve the throughput as well as maintain safety and efficiency.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Again, I refer to my earlier speech when I talked about Distributed Multi-Nodal Air Traffic Flow management.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I apologise; it has only been one week since I have been doing this.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The speed with which this can be implemented will have to vary according to the comfort level, as well as to how familiar and how constructive and positive the relationship is.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I would also draw reference to an earlier concept of a Seamless ASEAN sky.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Again, the concept is that it is possible for win-win outcomes to be formulated using technology so long as we get the diplomacy and the foreign relations right.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: That is why we are focused on very intense, very delicate discussions and negotiations with our counterparts.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I hope Members also understand that not all of this can be made public.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: A lot of these discussions are best conducted quietly, behind closed doors.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Give CAAS and the authorities some more time.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Changi Airport, air services and, in fact, the logistics, the air logistics, are a very significant sector for us economically.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We must do our best to protect it, to nurture it and to promote it.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But the point I also want to make to our neighbours is that this is an area where we can engage in win-win collaboration and not zero-sum games.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Mr Chairman, Mr Dennis Tan asked about the need for diesel tax as a nudge towards achieving LTMP 2040 goals given that we in the Government have committed to a clean public bus fleet and the taxi operators have already committed.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I hope the Member agrees, firstly, that achieving a cleaner vehicular fleet is important for our personal health and the health of our city.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: That is not going to happen without some nudges and some economic incentives.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It is not an easy decision to make.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There are some costs and some difficulties associated with that.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We need to start moving in that direction today and not wait until 2040 to find out whether we are moving in the right direction or not, or whether we have gotten there.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Thirdly, diesel is not only used in taxis today.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We have commercial vehicles, goods vehicles and private buses as well.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And so, this is an important part of the vehicle population and we will have to persuade the owners, drivers and operators of these vehicles to move along with us on this journey towards a cleaner fleet by 2040.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The first is on the criteria for selecting the PMD operators.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In fact, LTA will consider each application on its own merits based the following criteria.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will look at the company's track record.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We look at whether they will be able to be compliant with the law and regulatory requirements, whether there are plans to educate users on safe riding behaviours and, at the same time, we also look at the overall demands for shared services and the availability of parking spaces.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But having said that, we also need to take errant riders to task.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: An individual will actually be penalised under the existing active mobility regulations.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With regard to the Member's second question on the 1996 Limitation on Liability, I remember we had just passed the Merchants Shipping amendments only in January this year, which was just two months ago.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And MPA is currently looking at the implementation timeline with relevant agencies, and we will update the Member as soon as we have the details.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Mr Chairman, just a quick clarification with Senior Minister of State Lam Pin Min.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Sorry if I did not make myself clear.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: My question on PMD is really on whether the errant behaviour of hirers will be taken into account when LTA assesses whether or not the relevant operator has complied with the licence operating conditions.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: That means, after the licence has been awarded, will the errant behaviour of their hirers be taken against them, so to speak?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Also, in respect of their hirers' eligibility to continue to hire with any of the commercial operators.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: So, will errant behaviour, let us say, if this rider has been caught riding on the road when he is not supposed to, will that actually be taken against him?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Because if that is a case, then it will deter errant behaviour, just like what we see with shared bikes.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Yes, it depends on the circumstance whereby the errant rider has gone against the active mobility regulations and requirements.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But, of course, we look at the operator's efforts in educating users on safe riding behaviour and this will be taken into consideration.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: It will not be exactly fair to just penalise the operator if the operator has done its best to educate users with regard to safe riding behaviour.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: I am sure my residents are monitoring the emergency flights.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: I have one question for Senior Minister State Lam Pin Min and one question for Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey Yam Keng.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: My next question is: is LTA open to allowing Town Councils to take on this role of taking enforcement action at town centres where there are potential hazards?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: My question to Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey Yam Keng is that, talking about approval timeframe by LTA, I am sure LTA officers are all working very hard, trying their very best, but is the Senior Parliamentary Secretary open for dialogue sessions with architects and engineers to hear their side of the problems that they are facing, because I constantly receive feedback that the approval process is very long-drawn, one written direction after another written direction?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Perhaps, the Senior Parliamentary Secretary might like to have a dialogue session with the professionals.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Mr Chairman, I just want to thank Er Dr Lee Bee Wah on her supplementary questions.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In fact, we have discussed this issue in previous Parliamentary Sittings.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And the Active Mobility Act allows pedestrians, cyclists and PMD users to use such footpaths as they are crucial for connectivity.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I have explained in my speech just now that it is also important for these same rules to be applied consistently to all footpaths so that users will not be confused with different rules at different areas.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For example, if you do allow a certain area in a certain Town Council to have a no cycling zone but allow cycling in other Town Councils, PMD users or cyclists may not be aware that it is not allowed and that will cause confusion.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA will continue to work with Town Councils to assess the areas of concern and see whether we can have additional mitigating measures, such as infrastructure works or better education and engagement efforts, so that the safety concerns can be addressed.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For example, if we know that there is a particular hotspot that may be prone to incidents, then we can have signages to warn PMD users, we can have signages to warn pedestrians.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: At the same time, we can also have CCTVs installed to enforce or to catch errant riders in those areas.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA, together with MOT, is committed to working with the Town Council of Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and we can have joint education programmes as well as enforcement actions to make sure that the hotspot that she is alluding to can be addressed in a timely manner.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: On Er Dr Lee Bee Wah's question, as a regulator, the Government plays a role in meeting the needs of various stakeholders, including end consumers, users of public transport and the industry.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Public safety, the interests of the public as well as business commercial interests will have to be balanced.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Maybe I would just like to ask Er Dr Lee Bee Wah when she talked about architects and engineers, is it in any particular area under LTA's or any of our Statutory Boards' purview?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: For any new project, architects and engineers will have to make plan submissions, including to LTA and the Building and Construction Authority (BCA) and many other Government agencies.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: So, when we talk about productivity, we hope that we can work together to see how best to expedite the approval rather than a lot of resubmissions that cause a lot of time delay.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I believe Mr Chan Chun Sing, in his earlier speech, had talked about how the Public Service should adapt with changing times and technologies but, at the same time, balancing the different needs of various stakeholders.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: Currently, I understand that it is limited by statute to just advising on public rail, bus and taxi specifically.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: So, I seek his view on whether it is appropriate to include other P2P services for a start, but eventually, also active mobility services where balancing the interests of stakeholders and commuters is very important.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: And, if not, then what are the Ministry's plans for overseeing or advising on these emerging services in general?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Assoc Prof Walter Theseira for his suggestions.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, when we are looking across the industry, we are working together, with LTA as a regulator and the PTC looking out for fare affordability and services to citizens.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In the Member's earlier speech, he made comments about integrating services, for example.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There are a number of aspects to integrating services.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There is a regulatory component which LTA does take on, in terms of how we might integrate different aspects of our regulatory framework.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There is a working relationship that appears to be working quite well.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Perhaps, as new models of public transport or as new models of P2P, business operations or integrated services come along, we will continue to study and try to find the right response.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But I take the Member's point that we need an integrated series of solutions to link the different modalities of transport together.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: Mr Chairman, there was a report in the Straits Times yesterday about NTU and Volvo launching an autonomous electric bus that is 12 metres long.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: I noted that Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary has mentioned that AVs are still a long way away from our roads.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: But can I ask, does MOT have a rough timeline as to when such AVs can be on our roads?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Those vehicles, the operators that do that, have already pretested these in facilities like the Centre of Excellence for Testing and Research of AVs-NTU at NTU, to establish the basic safety.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The issue of autonomous cars – so, there are two different types of AVs – autonomous cars for private vehicle ownership, we do not have a timeline at the moment but we are actively engaging with the industry, we have made calls for proposals and we are working with a number of partners to establish what are the regulatory changes that we need, what is the local capability that we need.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And perhaps, in the future Land Transport Master Plan, we might be able to announce something.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But at the moment, we do not have a timeline for that.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, clear timeline for revenue service for autonomous buses; at the moment, no timeline for autonomous cars.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin, would you like to withdraw your amendment, please?

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: Chairman, I would like to thank all speakers and the entire MOT team for their hard work.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: With that, Mr Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
